THE SENDABLE PO STATUSES VERSUS THE PURCHASE-CONSIGNMENT VALID SET, differing by CANCELLED — you may not email a cancelled PO, but CANCELLED is still a legal PCO status. Two questions.
THE SO STATUS RANK VERSUS THE AR STATUSES, differing by CLOSED/DRAFT. A rank table needs every status; AR needs the ones that can still carry a balance.
TWO SUBSETS OF ONE VOCABULARY differing by COLOURCODE; the smaller side is a filtered view (one screen's options, one agent's interest), not a competing definition.

DELIVERABLE_FROM VERSUS CANCELLABLE_STATUSES, differing by SHIPPED — the point at which a DO may be cut is exactly the point at which the SO stops being cancellable. Adjacent by design, opposite in meaning.
THE ARRANGEMENT-STAGE SPLIT VERSUS ITS LABEL MAP, differing by DATE_ARRANGED. arrangement-stage.ts records that the date side and the time side name the same stage differently on purpose.

THE CREW-SCOPED POSITIONS VERSUS THE SIDEBAR'S HIDE LIST, differing by DRIVER — and that is deliberate: projectGates.ts says drivers stay unscoped on the projects list, while the sidebar hides the Assistant from drivers too. Two questions, one member apart. The crew predicate itself is PINNED by backend/tests/duplicatedDecisionPins.test.ts against the frontend's copy.

TWO UPLOAD WHITELISTS differing by DWG/SKP. Each surface decides what it accepts and they are not required to agree; the difference here is the surface (a supplier portal takes no DWG, the ops app takes video).
THE MAIL OUTBOX STATUSES VERSUS THE AUTOCOUNT OUTBOX STATUSES, differing by SKIPPED. Two different outboxes for two different systems that happen to share four state names. Not one rule.

TWO UPLOAD WHITELISTS differing by IMAGE/GIF. Each surface decides what it accepts and they are not required to agree; the difference here is the surface (a supplier portal takes no DWG, the ops app takes video).

TWO UPLOAD WHITELISTS differing by MOV/WEBM. Each surface decides what it accepts and they are not required to agree; the difference here is the surface (a supplier portal takes no DWG, the ops app takes video).
TWO SIDEBAR ENTRIES' ACCESS LISTS differing by PROJECTS.FINANCES. One nav item additionally needs the finances grant. Not a rule with two homes.

THE SOFA-MIX RULE IS NOT ENFORCED ON THE SERVER FOR CONSIGNMENT ORDERS. soMainMixIntroduced guards BOTH the add and the edit path of a sales order; the consignment routes have no copy, while ConsignmentOrderNew.tsx enforces the rule client-side via hasSofaMixConflict — which exists only in the vendored frontend so-variant-rule.ts and has no backend counterpart. So the rule is enforced at the form and nowhere behind it. Recorded and NOT fixed here: whether a consignment order may mix a sofa with a bedframe is the owner's call, and adding a server refusal is a behaviour change, not a gate. This entry is the dated question.

THE CREW-SCOPED POSITIONS, and this twin is DELIBERATE: the projects filter bar has to render before any round-trip, so the client cannot wait to be told. It is also the twin that had already drifted — the desktop copy substring-matched the position name and carried no permission escape, so an owner-created "Warehouse Helper" caged the UI while the server returned everything, and an admin holding the Storekeeper position lost controls the server would have allowed. PINNED by backend/tests/duplicatedDecisionPins.test.ts, which imports BOTH implementations and runs one corpus of (position, permissions) pairs through them. Added by the same change that created the second home — this gate flagged its own author, which is the behaviour it is for.
